The name ATA_QCFLAG_FAILED is misleading since it does not mean that a
QC completed in error
column2: or that it didn't complete at all. It means that

column1: libata decided to schedule EH for the QC
column2: so the QC is now owned by the

column1: libata error handler (EH).
The normal execution path is responsible for not accessing a QC owned
by EH. libata core enforces the rule by returning NULL from
ata_qc_from_tag() for QCs owned by EH.
It is quite easy to mistake that a QC marked with ATA_QCFLAG_FAILED was
an error. However
column2: a QC that was actually an error is instead indicated

column1: by having qc->err_mask set. E.g. when we have a NCQ error
QCs
column2: which currently will mark all QCs as ATA_QCFLAG_FAILED. However

column1: will only be a single QC that is an error (i.e. has qc->err_mask set).
Rename ATA_QCFLAG_FAILED to ATA_QCFLAG_EH to more clearly highlight that
this flag simply means that a QC is now owned by EH. This new name will
not mislead to think that the QC was an error (which is instead
indicated by having qc->err_mask set).
This also makes it more obvious that the EH code skips all QCs that do
not have ATA_QCFLAG_EH set (rather than ATA_QCFLAG_FAILED)
code should simply only care about QCs that are owned by EH itself.
